candidate.answerReason: Segment BE divides the displayed hexagon into two unit-sided parallelograms, each with height √3/2. Their combined area is √3.

methods.label: Split the figure into two parallelograms
methods.explanation:
Join \(B\) to \(E\). This divides the displayed figure into quadrilaterals \(ABEF\) and \(BCDE\), whose areas we can add.

Because \(AB\) and \(FE\) are parallel and both have length \(1\), \(ABEF\) is a parallelogram: one pair of opposite sides is both parallel and equal. Likewise, \(BC\) and \(ED\) show that \(BCDE\) is a parallelogram. Each has adjacent sides of length \(1\) and an included angle of \(60^\circ\), at \(A\) and \(C\), respectively.

To find the height of either parallelogram, consider two unit sides meeting at \(60^\circ\). Joining their other endpoints forms an equilateral triangle of side \(1\). Its altitude bisects the opposite side, so the Pythagorean theorem gives the height
\[
h=\sqrt{1^2-\left(\frac12\right)^2}
=\frac{\sqrt3}{2}.
\]
Thus each parallelogram has area \(1\cdot h=\sqrt3/2\). The two pieces fill the hexagon and share only their boundary \(BE\), so the required area is
\[
\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt3}{2}
=\boxed{\sqrt3},
\]
choice \(\boxed{D}\).
methods.levelReason: The solution uses a geometric decomposition, the base-times-height area formula, and an equilateral-triangle altitude derived by the Pythagorean theorem. Trigonometry is unnecessary.
